fix(B1/B2): gate hosted MCP server on subscription (revenue leak)

* fix(B1/B2): gate hosted MCP server on subscription (was 100% free)

The hosted MCP server authenticated by API-key EXISTENCE only — anyone who
ever ran connect had the full product free forever (total revenue leak).
Add server/entitlement.ts: assertEntitled(userId) reads user_subscriptions
(single source of truth, Stripe-synced), evaluated at the one choke point
every transport shares — handleMCPMessage → tools/call. initialize and
tools/list stay free so the handshake never blocks.

Two safety rules, both live-verified against prod DB:
- Get-or-create trial: register-repo never seeded a user_subscriptions row,
  so a strict switch would lock out every trial user (the refund fear).
  First gated call seeds a 7-day trial (check_user_exists constraint allows
  users/auth.users/cli_users owners — CLI users included). No Stripe call on
  the gate path.
- Fail closed: lookup error → deny with a retryable message, never grant.

Verified live (real cli_user id): new→trial(7d), expired→trial_expired,
active/professional→paid, cancelled→payment_required, bad-lookup→denied.


* fix(gate): close all revenue-leak paths in hosted MCP subscription gate

Adversarial review of the first pass found the gate insufficient: only
tools/call was gated, and it seeded a fresh user_subscriptions trial —
a third, divergent trial system open to reseed abuse and key drift.

Rework: server/entitlement.ts is now a single reconciled, READ-ONLY
entitlement used by every product path.
  - PAID  = user_subscriptions (Stripe source of truth): active|past_due
            with a paid plan. past_due honored as a dunning grace window
            so a transient card failure never hard-locks a payer.
  - TRIAL = the clock registration actually writes
            (users/cli_users.trial_ends_at, default NOW()+7d). Never
            created or reset here — no reseed, no divergence.
  - Fail CLOSED on any lookup error (never grant on unverifiable state).

Coverage — every product-data path now gated:
  - mcp-sse.ts: tools/call, prompts/get, resources/read (via shared
    paymentRequiredError helper, JSON-RPC -32003). initialize / *_list
    stay free so the handshake and capability discovery never block.
  - mcp-memory.ts: all 7 /v1/memory/* endpoints via requireEntitled
    (auth+gate). 5 of them (sync-tools, capture-pattern, capture-decision,
    stats, list) previously had NO auth at all — closed.
  - index.ts: registerMCPProtocol UNMOUNTED — its /mcp/tools/call ran
    memory tools with no auth and no gate (tenant-isolation hole); dead
    legacy duplicate, referenced by no client.

Live-verified against prod DB: new/future trial → allow; expired trial
→ deny (no row created); paid → allow; past_due → allow (grace);
cancelled → deny; lookup error → deny. 230 jest pass, tsc clean.


* fix(gate): close ai-learning + CLI-sync leaks; honor past_due/trialing (refund risk)

Second adversarial pass on the gate found three more product surfaces
mounted next to the ones just fixed, plus two refund-risk status bugs.

Revenue leaks closed (authed-but-ungated = expired user with a valid key
still got the full product):
  - /v1/ai-learning/* (16 handlers): the decisions/context/errors/
    preferences/impact/docs product the Python + JS SDKs call. Was
    requireAuth-only. Now requireEntitled.
  - /v1/projects/:id/* + /v1/analyze/* (16 routes): the CLI's git-sync,
    entities/relationships bulk, patterns, file-context, auto-capture,
    sync-trigger, plus ROI/summary/history reads. Was requireAuth-only.
    Now requireEntitled. Ownership checks were already present.

New shared gate: server/index.ts exports requireEntitled(req, reply) =
requireAuth + assertEntitled (401 / 402), mirroring mcp-memory's helper.

Refund-risk fixes (a real payer was being denied):
  - requireAuth no longer hard-denies `past_due` — that's a dunning grace
    window owned by assertEntitled, so a transient card failure keeps a
    paying customer authenticated instead of 401-locking them mid-retry.
    Still denies `cancelled` (a truly dead account).
  - assertEntitled honors Stripe `trialing` (a real trial on a paid plan:
    coupon / trial_period_days), guarded by a paid plan_id so a bare/
    free_trial row can't self-grant.

Deliberately left ungated (freemium boundary): project metadata CRUD and
raw spec/plan/event/time-entry storage — you can put inputs in, but
extracting AI value (memory intelligence, context fusion, ai-learning)
requires an active subscription. Auth/registration/subscription/telemetry
routes stay identity-only so onboarding never breaks.

NOT fixed here (separate class — unauth/IDOR, needs internal-caller auth):
/v1/evolution/* and /v1/self-healing/* are mounted with ZERO auth and some
return tenant data. Tracked for a focused security PR.

Live-verified (prod DB): trialing/past_due/active+paid plan → paid;
trialing/active + free_trial plan → not paid (falls to trial clock);
cancelled → deny; new/future trial → allow, expired → deny, no reseed.
Also confirmed current_period_start/end + plan_id are NOT NULL (why the
A1 Basil period fix matters — a null-period write fails the insert and
locks the payer). tsc clean, 230 jest pass.

fix(security): unmount unauthenticated /v1/evolution/* and /v1/self-healing/*

Adversarial review of the subscription gate surfaced two more surfaces
mounted on the hosted server that authenticated NOTHING:

  /v1/evolution/*  — every route read/wrote tenant data keyed by a
    body/param projectId with no auth and no ownership check:
    POST /fuse-contexts returned any project's `memories`;
    GET /population/:projectId and /agents/:projectId/stats returned any
    project's agents; /metrics/:projectId returned evolution_metrics;
    POST /workflow/execute and /agent/execute ran arbitrary AI work
    against any project. Cross-tenant data disclosure + unmetered
    execution reachable by an anonymous caller who knows a project UUID.

  /v1/self-healing/* — unauthenticated privileged ops control: heal,
    monitor start/stop, add/remove monitored services, system metrics
    and history.

Both are experimental surfaces with NO production caller:
  - lib/hallucination-evolution-pipeline (the evolve-agent caller) is
    invoked nowhere.
  - lib/self-healing/system-monitor (the health-check caller) is invoked
    nowhere.
  - the EvolutionDashboard component is imported by no page.
  - the Next proxy routes app/api/evolution/* ARE properly authenticated
    (requireProjectAccess / requireApiAuth with ownership) and read the DB
    directly — they never needed the Fastify endpoints; unmounting only
    404s a dead fetch in an unrendered feature.

Same treatment registerMCPProtocol got: unmount rather than leave an
unauthenticated tenant-data hole on a public server. Re-mounting requires
requireEntitled + getProject() ownership (evolution) and admin/service
auth (self-healing) — documented at the mount site.

tsc clean. server/index.ts is eslint-ignored (no lint impact).

problem_statement:
feat(payments): webhook idempotency + reconciliation + payment ledger (A2/A3/A4)

* feat(payments): webhook idempotency + post-payment reconciliation + payment ledger

Makes payment collection robust so a duplicated, delayed, or missed Stripe
webhook never means a double-processed event or a locked-out paying
customer. (Workstream A: A2/A3/A4.)

A2 — Webhook idempotency (new stripe_events table + migration)
  Stripe delivers at-least-once and retries on any non-2xx for ~3 days.
  handleWebhook now skips any event id it has already fully processed, and
  records the id only AFTER the handler succeeds — so a transient failure is
  reprocessed on retry (handlers are idempotent) while a duplicate of an
  already-handled event is a no-op. Live-verified against prod DB: duplicate
  skipped pre-dispatch, fresh event recorded, re-delivery a no-op.

A3 — Post-payment reconciliation (new app/api/stripe/reconcile route)
  The success redirect carries the checkout session id; the dashboard now
  POSTs it to /api/stripe/reconcile, which retrieves the session straight
  from the Stripe API and, only if genuinely paid, upserts the subscription.
  So a customer gets access the moment they return from Checkout even if the
  webhook is delayed, dropped, or STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET isn't set yet — the
  belt-and-suspenders against "I paid but I'm locked out" refunds. Shared
  upsertSubscriptionFromCheckout() backs both webhook and reconcile paths.
  Also fixed a real bug: success_url appended `?session_id=` after the
  caller's existing `?success=true`, folding the id into that value and
  making it unretrievable — now uses the correct `&` separator.

A4 — Payment ledger
  handlePaymentSucceeded now writes payment_history idempotently
  (UNIQUE stripe_invoice_id), wrapped so a ledger failure never wedges the
  webhook. This is the record to adjudicate any refund/dispute against.

Tests: 3 new reconcile unit tests (unpaid → no activation; paid → activate;
complete-status honored) + idempotency live-verified. 236 jest pass, tsc
clean, lint 0 errors.

OWNER ACTIONS (blocking real charges — I cannot do these):
  - The Stripe test key in Doppler (prd) is EXPIRED — rotate it; no test
    payment can be created/verified until then.
  - Create the Stripe webhook endpoint and set STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET.
    (Reconciliation works without it, but the webhook is the primary path.)


* fix(payments): reconcile must require PAID+complete+recent — close free/replay activation

Adversarial review of this PR caught money-critical bugs in the reconcile
path I introduced. Fixes:

C1/C2 (CRITICAL — free activation): the paid-check was an OR
(`payment_status !== 'paid' && status !== 'complete'`), so it activated
whenever a session was paid OR complete. A subscription Checkout Session can
be status:'complete' while payment_status is 'unpaid' or
'no_payment_required' (SCA pending, async payment, trial, 100%-off coupon) —
Stripe has NO money — yet it would write an active subscription. Now a strict
AND: mode==='subscription' && payment_status==='paid' && status==='complete'.
Webhooks handle the settle-later transitions.

C3 (CRITICAL — replay): a Checkout Session stays paid/complete forever, so an
old success URL in browser history could be re-POSTed to re-activate a
since-cancelled subscription. Added a recency guard — only sessions created
within 24h reconcile; anything older is a webhook's job.

M3 (un-cancel): handlePaymentSucceeded hardcoded status:'active', so a late
invoice.payment_succeeded (e.g. final proration invoice, out-of-order
delivery) could flip a legitimately canceled/past_due sub back to active. Now
writes the subscription's actual current status.

L2: guard invoice.id before the ledger upsert (it's the dedup key and typed
string|undefined).

My earlier test "treats a complete-status session as paid" ENSHRINED C1 — it
is deleted and replaced with 5 tests that assert the correct denials
(complete-but-unpaid, no_payment_required, old session) and the one activation
(recent+paid+complete). 242 jest pass, tsc clean.

Residual (documented, low impact): the reconcile route is unauthenticated (the
browser uses localStorage auth, not the server cookies requireApiAuth needs)
and unrate-limited. Impact is bounded: activation only ever targets the paid
session's own metadata userId, and now only for a recent, genuinely-paid
session. Serverless rate limiting needs Upstash (not wired) — tracked.

+import { NextRequest, NextResponse } from 'next/server'
+import { subscriptionService } from '@/lib/subscription'
+
+/**
+ * Post-checkout reconciliation.
+ *
+ * The Stripe "success" redirect lands here (via the dashboard) carrying the
+ * checkout session id. We retrieve the session straight from the Stripe API
+ * and, if it's genuinely paid, upsert user_subscriptions immediately — so the
+ * customer has access the moment they return, even if the webhook is delayed,
+ * dropped, or STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET isn't configured yet. This is the
+ * belt-and-suspenders that stops "I paid but I'm locked out" refund tickets.
+ *
+ * Auth model: the session id is a Stripe-issued capability (cs_...), and the
+ * write target is the userId baked into the session's metadata at creation —
+ * NOT the caller. So this only ever activates the subscription that was
+ * actually paid for; there's nothing to escalate by calling it.
+ */
+export const runtime = 'nodejs'
+
+export async function POST(request: NextRequest) {
+  try {
+    const { session_id } = await request.json().catch(() => ({ session_id: undefined }))
+    if (!session_id || typeof session_id !== 'string') {
+      return NextResponse.json({ error: 'session_id required' }, { status: 400 })
+    }
+
+    const result = await subscriptionService.reconcileCheckoutSession(session_id)
+    if (!result.ok) {
+      // Not-yet-paid is a normal transient state, not a server error.
+      return NextResponse.json({ activated: false, reason: result.reason }, { status: 200 })
+    }
+    return NextResponse.json({ activated: true, status: result.status, planId: result.planId })
+  } catch (error) {
+    console.error('Reconcile error:', error)
+    return NextResponse.json({ error: 'reconcile_failed' }, { status: 500 })
+  }
+}

* fix(onboarding): native-HTTP configs + spec-correct SSE handshake + real verification

Fixes the "just says connecting" hang end to end (Workstream C: C1/C2/C3).

native-HTTP callers. Both POST paths now 202 notifications (no id) instead of
falling through to a JSON-RPC error mid-handshake.

Closes the tracked cross-identity gap. A user who CONNECTS via the CLI

account row (email + trial clock) is fetched once and reused.

   paid_at from the invoice), and now `if (ledgerErr) throw ledgerErr` so any future
   mismatch surfaces via the catch instead of silently dropping ledger rows.

The hosted MCP server trusted the client-supplied X-Project-Id header as
PRIORITY 1 and resolved the caller's userId from the API token independently,
never checking that the token owner actually owns the named project. With
lib/memory-service.ts scoping every read/write by project_id ALONE (no user_id
co-filter) and no ownership check in the tool-dispatch path, any valid vm_ key
plus an arbitrary X-Project-Id could read or write another tenant's memory

project. Enforce it in BOTH transport entry points (POST /mcp/sse and
POST /mcp/messages) after userId+projectId resolve and before dispatch,
returning 403 with an actionable message. Access model mirrors the Next.js
requireProjectAccess guard; deliberately not email-linked (that stays a
billing concern in entitlement.ts — a security ACL stays strict).

(line 97) — verify it validates ownership before querying.

+import { supabaseServer } from './db-supabase'

+/**
+ * Cross-tenant authorization guard for the hosted MCP transport.
+ *
+ * The X-Project-Id header is client-controlled and the caller's `userId` is
+ * resolved from the API token INDEPENDENTLY of it. Without this check any valid
+ * key could name any project in the header and read/write its memories —
+ * `lib/memory-service.ts` scopes every query by `project_id` ALONE (no
+ * `user_id` co-filter), so the data layer is no second line of defense. That is
+ * a cross-tenant IDOR on the core memory brain.

+ * project OWNER (`projects.user_id`) or a member of the project's team
+ * (`projects.team_id` → `team_members`). Deliberately NOT email-linked — that
+ * is a billing concern (`server/entitlement.ts`); a security ACL stays strict.
+ * A same-person cross-identity setup should use a matched-pair config (the
+ * project's own key) or a shared team, never a silent identity bridge.
+ *
+ * Fails CLOSED: any lookup error or missing project denies.
+ */
+export async function userCanAccessProject(userId: string, projectId: string): Promise<boolean> {
+  try {
+    const { data: project, error } = await supabaseServer
+      .from('projects')
+      .select('user_id, team_id')
+      .eq('id', projectId)
+      .maybeSingle()
+    if (error || !project) return false
+    if (project.user_id === userId) return true

+        .from('team_members')
+        .select('user_id')
+        .eq('team_id', project.team_id)
+        .eq('user_id', userId)
+        .maybeSingle()
+      if (member) return true
+    }
+    return false
+  } catch {
+    return false
+  }

Root cause of the duplicate-data / "data gaps": identity lives in two tables
(users, cli_users) with no link, and the registration paths diverged —
/api/register looked ONLY at cli_users, so a person who already had a web account
got a parallel CLI identity minted, splitting their projects/memories across two
ids. The MCP then wrote an empty shadow project while the dashboard showed the
real one.

  registration path; ALWAYS prefers an existing web `users` row over cli_users,
  creates a cli_user only if neither exists (case-insensitive email, matching the
  billing layer's cross-identity linking in server/entitlement.ts).

  across ALL ids sharing the email, so connect never mints a duplicate under a
  sibling identity.

  (this was the leak); return the existing project for existing accounts.
- app/api/auth/register-repo/route.ts: use the resolver + cross-identity project
  reuse.
- packages/cli connect: scope registration + doc discovery to the GIT REPO ROOT

  running from a parent/home dir and cross-pollinating one project's memory with

dupes were always blocked; the shadows were cross-identity, which the resolver now
prevents. No schema change.

+import { SupabaseClient } from '@supabase/supabase-js'
+import { randomUUID } from 'crypto'

+export type IdentitySource = 'users' | 'cli_users' | 'new'
+
+export interface ResolvedUser {
+  userId: string
+  source: IdentitySource
+  /** Existing api key when the account was found; a freshly minted one when created. */
+  apiKey: string | null
+}
+
+/**
+ * Resolve a caller's CANONICAL identity by email, creating one only if none
+ * exists. ALWAYS prefers an existing web `users` row over a `cli_users` row —
+ * the web row is the canonical account (it carries billing, roles, and is the
+ * identity the dashboard authenticates as).
+ *
+ * This is the fix for the shadow-identity bug: `/api/register` previously looked
+ * ONLY at `cli_users`, so a person who already had a web account got a parallel
+ * CLI identity minted, splitting their projects/memories across two ids. Routing
+ * every registration path through this one resolver makes that impossible.
+ *
+ * Email is matched case-insensitively — the same loose key the billing layer
+ * uses (server/entitlement.ts lookupLinkedPaidSub).
+ */
+export async function resolveOrCreateUser(
+  supabase: SupabaseClient,
+  email: string
+): Promise<ResolvedUser> {
+  const e = email.toLowerCase()
+
+  const { data: webUser } = await supabase
+    .from('users')
+    .select('id, api_key')
+    .ilike('email', e)
+    .maybeSingle()
+  if (webUser) return { userId: webUser.id, source: 'users', apiKey: webUser.api_key ?? null }
+
+  const { data: cliUser } = await supabase
+    .from('cli_users')
+    .select('id, api_key')
+    .ilike('email', e)
+    .maybeSingle()
+  if (cliUser) return { userId: cliUser.id, source: 'cli_users', apiKey: cliUser.api_key ?? null }
+
+  const userId = randomUUID()
+  const apiKey = `vm_${userId.substring(0, 8)}_${randomUUID().replace(/-/g, '').substring(0, 16)}`
+  const { error } = await supabase.from('cli_users').insert({
+    id: userId,
+    email: e,
+    api_key: apiKey,
+    subscription_tier: 'free',
+    subscription_status: 'active',
+    metadata: { source: 'cli-auto-registration', registeredAt: new Date().toISOString() },
+  })
+  if (error) throw new Error(`resolveOrCreateUser: failed to create user: ${error.message}`)
+  return { userId, source: 'new', apiKey }
+}
+
+export interface LinkedProject {
+  id: string
+  api_key: string
+  name: string
+  user_id: string
+}
+
+/**
+ * Find an existing project for this repo slug across EVERY identity that shares
+ * the email (web `users` + `cli_users`), not just the caller's own id. This is
+ * what lets a CLI connect reuse the web-identity project instead of creating a
+ * duplicate under a sibling id. Returns the project or null.
+ */
+export async function findProjectBySlugForEmail(
+  supabase: SupabaseClient,
+  email: string,
+  slug: string
+): Promise<LinkedProject | null> {
+  const e = email.toLowerCase()
+  const [web, cli] = await Promise.all([
+    supabase.from('users').select('id').ilike('email', e),
+    supabase.from('cli_users').select('id').ilike('email', e),
+  ])
+  const ids = [
+    ...(((web.data as { id: string }[] | null) ?? []).map((r) => r.id)),
+    ...(((cli.data as { id: string }[] | null) ?? []).map((r) => r.id)),
+  ]
+  if (ids.length === 0) return null
+
+  const { data } = await supabase
+    .from('projects')
+    .select('id, api_key, name, user_id')
+    .in('user_id', ids)
+    .eq('slug', slug)
+    .limit(1)
+  return data && data[0] ? (data[0] as LinkedProject) : null
+}

problem_statement:
fix(cloud): git/codebase functions must not scan the server's process.cwd()

On the hosted (Railway/Vercel) MCP server, process.cwd() is the DEPLOY
directory, not the caller's repo. Three lib/codebase-intelligence.ts functions
fell back to `projectPath || process.cwd()` with no cloud guard, and the SSE
server calls them WITHOUT a projectPath — so over the cloud MCP they operated on
the server's own filesystem/git:

- syncGitHistory: ran `git log` in the deploy dir and wrote THIS server's commits
  into the caller's brain as if they were the caller's project history
  (active data pollution).
- getRecentChanges: returned the server's git as the caller's recent changes.
- getRelatedFiles: filesystem fallback grep/ls'd the deploy dir, returning this
  repo's files as "related".

Fix: filesystem/git access now requires an EXPLICIT projectPath. Without one
(cloud), syncGitHistory/getRecentChanges return an honest "run `vasperamemory
sync` locally" result and getRelatedFiles returns the DB-backed result — never a
process.cwd() scan. get_codebase_summary was already cloud-safe (DB branch).
No local behavior change: these functions have no local (stdio) callers; only the
cloud SSE server calls them, always without a path.

Test: __tests__/codebase-intelligence-cloud.test.ts (jest, 2 passing).

fix(security): remove unauth debug routes; enforce plan quotas on write paths

Two production liabilities from the competitive/code audit.

1. SECURITY — removed two unauthenticated, service-role debug endpoints:
   - app/api/debug/db-check: leaked env presence, row counts, AND a full raw
     memory row (content) to anyone, unauthenticated, via the service-role client.
   - app/api/test-db: leaked env presence.
   Neither is referenced anywhere.

2. QUOTAS — plan limits were never enforced on any write path (a free/over-limit
   user could create unlimited memories and projects via API/MCP). Now enforced,
   FAIL-OPEN (a transient resolution error never blocks a legitimate write;
   entitlement remains the real access gate — quota only blocks a genuine
   over-limit where a finite limit resolved):
   - checkUsageLimit is now trial-aware: trial users (no user_subscriptions row,
     gated by the trial clock) resolve to free_trial limits instead of 'none', so
     enforcement never hard-blocks a trialing user. Added isWithinTrial().
   - captureMemory (the single choke point for all memory writes — mcp-memory,
     git-learning, stdio/http, lsp) rejects over-limit with QuotaExceededError.
   - register-repo and projects.createProject reject over the project limit (402).

Not addressed here (belongs in the pricing spec): the free_trial limits are still
more generous than Starter/Professional — that's a plan-numbers decision, not an
enforcement bug.

(title/content/reasoning/status/confidence) — a direct violation of "Never

versioning subsystem is unwired from the UI — no frontend caller) are kept for
continuity. no-bypass.test.ts drops the restore route from the content allowlist.

problem_statement:
fix(dashboard): default to the project with data + remember last selection

Users with multiple projects could open the dashboard onto an empty project (e.g.
"Shadow-Engine", 0 memories) and think their data was gone — the multi-project
"wrong brain" trap. The old selection logic only considered "vaspera"-named
projects, ranked them with stale-closure `!selectedProject` guards, and fell back
to the first *connected* project (which can be empty). Nothing was persisted.

- Restore the user's last-selected project from localStorage on load (persist it
  in handleProjectSelect), so returning users reopen the project they were using.
- When nothing is persisted, default to the project with the MOST memories across
  ALL projects — applied in the memory-counts effect using the same reliable
  server-side counts the selector displays (/api/projects/[id]/metrics). Falls
  back to a connected project, then the first, only when all are empty.
- Removed the vaspera-only filter, the stale `!selectedProject` guards, and the
  empty-first-connected fallback; kept default-project creation for new users.

No data was ever lost — this only changes which project the dashboard opens.
tsc clean; production build succeeds.

fix(dashboard): make user-role assignment idempotent (onConflict user_id)

assignUserRole called .upsert() WITHOUT an onConflict target, so it conflict-
matched the default primary key (a fresh id each call) and collided on the
user_roles_user_id_key UNIQUE constraint — throwing "duplicate key" on concurrent
dashboard loads / React double-invoke. loadDashboard caught it but then skipped
project loading on that pass. Target user_id so a repeat call updates instead of
failing.

Surfaced by the new local-Supabase e2e (dashboard-smoke logged the error).
Verified: with the fix, the dashboard specs pass with ZERO duplicate-key /
"Dashboard load error" log lines.

fix(security): retrieval reads decrypt api_key_enc, not plaintext — PR-4b part 2 (HIGH)

Complete the read side of the encrypt-at-rest cutover. PR-4b part 1 (#72)
populated api_key_enc on every write; this points retrieval at it so the
plaintext api_key column can be dropped (PR-5) without breaking auth/connect.

- lib/api-key.ts: add resolveApiKey(client,row) — decrypt api_key_enc via the
  service-role decrypt_api_key RPC, fall back to plaintext during the transition
  (fail-open: a decrypt outage can never break auth).
- Migrate every genuine retrieval site to resolveApiKey (select api_key_enc too):
  app/api/ai-learning/{context,decisions,impact} proxies, register-repo reuse
  path, lib/identity.resolveOrCreateUser, lib/projects.getOrCreateApiKey.
- Drop vestigial plaintext from hash-lookup selects that never used it

  removes the plaintext read entirely, better than decrypting.
- Write paths (getOrCreateApiKey create branch, regenerateApiKey) return the
  freshly generated key instead of reading it back.

the browser anon client (getOrCreateApiKey), which cannot call the service-role
decrypt RPC — it stays on the plaintext fallback until key display moves
server-side. Plaintext column MUST NOT be dropped before that.

fix(security): dashboard fetches API key server-side — PR-5 prerequisite (HIGH)

Unblocks dropping the plaintext api_key column. The dashboard + admin layout
read the key via the browser anon client (projectService.getOrCreateApiKey),
which can't call the service-role decrypt_api_key RPC — so it could only ever
return the plaintext column. Move that read server-side so the column can go.

- app/api/keys/route.ts (new): GET (get-or-create) + POST (regenerate),
  service-role, decrypts api_key_enc via resolveApiKey. Auth = the caller's
  Supabase session JWT (Bearer) — browser sessions send no cookies (CLAUDE.md).
- lib/api-auth.ts: getRequestUser/requireRequestAuth — validate a Bearer JWT via
  supabaseAdmin.auth.getUser, fall back to the SSR cookie session.
- lib/api-key-client.ts (new): fetchOrCreateApiKey/regenerateApiKey — client
  helpers that send the session token to /api/keys.
- Dashboard + admin layout call the route instead of the anon client.
- lib/projects.ts: delete the now-dead client-side getOrCreateApiKey/
  regenerateApiKey (guard comment against reintroducing a client-side key read).

After this, NO client path reads the plaintext key — PR-5 (DROP COLUMN) is safe.
Held for explicit confirmation per plan.

Verified: typecheck clean; e2e 22/22 (governance authenticates with the key the
new route returns — proves JWT-Bearer + decrypt end-to-end on local Supabase);

--- /dev/null
+++ b/app/api/keys/route.ts
@@ -0,0 +1,82 @@
+/**
+ * User API key — server-side get-or-create + regenerate.
+ *
+ * The dashboard used to read the key via the browser anon client
+ * (`projectService.getOrCreateApiKey`). That path can't call the service-role
+ * `decrypt_api_key` RPC, so it can only ever return the plaintext `api_key`
+ * column — which blocks dropping that column (PR-5). This route runs with the
+ * service role: it decrypts `api_key_enc` via `resolveApiKey`, so once every
+ * key is encrypted the plaintext column can go away without breaking the UI.
+ *
+ * Auth is the caller's Supabase session JWT (Bearer) — browser sessions send no
+ * cookies (see CLAUDE.md), so `requireRequestAuth` accepts the token the client
+ * reads from `authService.getCurrentSession()`.
+ */
+import { NextRequest, NextResponse } from 'next/server'
+import { randomBytes } from 'crypto'
+import { supabaseAdmin } from '@/lib/supabase'
+import { requireRequestAuth } from '@/lib/api-auth'
+import { hashApiKey, resolveApiKey } from '@/lib/api-key'
+
+// CSPRNG key — same format as lib/projects.generateApiKey (CONSTITUTION Security
+// Invariants: never SQL random()). The DB encrypt-on-write trigger populates
+// api_key_enc; we set api_key_hash here for auth lookups.
+function generateApiKey(): string {
+  return `vm_${randomBytes(32).toString('base64url')}`
+}
+
+async function persistNewKey(userId: string): Promise<string> {
+  const apiKey = generateApiKey()
+  const { error } = await supabaseAdmin!
+    .from('users')
+    .update({
+      api_key: apiKey,
+      api_key_hash: hashApiKey(apiKey),
+      api_key_created_at: new Date().toISOString(),
+    })
+    .eq('id', userId)
+  if (error) throw error
+  return apiKey
+}
+
+// GET — return the caller's key, minting one if they have none yet.
+export async function GET(request: NextRequest) {
+  if (!supabaseAdmin) {
+    return NextResponse.json({ error: 'Supabase admin client not available' }, { status: 500 })
+  }
+  const auth = await requireRequestAuth(request)
+  if (auth instanceof NextResponse) return auth
+
+  try {
+    const { data: userData } = await supabaseAdmin
+      .from('users')
+      .select('api_key, api_key_enc')
+      .eq('id', auth.userId)
+      .single()
+
+    let apiKey = await resolveApiKey(supabaseAdmin, userData)
+    if (!apiKey) apiKey = await persistNewKey(auth.userId)
+
+    return NextResponse.json({ apiKey })
+  } catch (error) {
+    console.error('GET /api/keys error:', error)
+    return NextResponse.json({ error: 'Failed to resolve API key' }, { status: 500 })
+  }
+}
+
+// POST — regenerate (invalidates the previous key).
+export async function POST(request: NextRequest) {
+  if (!supabaseAdmin) {
+    return NextResponse.json({ error: 'Supabase admin client not available' }, { status: 500 })
+  }
+  const auth = await requireRequestAuth(request)
+  if (auth instanceof NextResponse) return auth
+
+  try {
+    const apiKey = await persistNewKey(auth.userId)
+    return NextResponse.json({ apiKey })
+  } catch (error) {
+    console.error('POST /api/keys error:', error)
+    return NextResponse.json({ error: 'Failed to regenerate API key' }, { status: 500 })
+  }
+}

+async function authHeaders(): Promise<Record<string, string>> {

+  return token ? { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}` } : {}
